findings.highlight: My fault…? I see… So it is my fault
findings.evidenceJa: 逆ギレ…？そっか…逆ギレしてるんだ、わたし…？
findings.explanation: Koharu repeats Ako's term 逆ギレ—lashing out when accused or angrily turning blame back—and dazedly recognizes that this is how her laughter looks. The English instead makes her accept that the whole situation is her fault, replacing her stunned recognition of her own emotional behavior with a direct confession of culpability.
findings.japanese:
「逆ギレ…？
そっか…逆ギレしてるんだ、わたし…？」
findings.todokanai: "My fault…? I see… So it is my fault…"

findings.highlight: so I just couldn't resist answering your call
findings.evidenceJa: 電話で雑談するの、本当に久しぶりだから勝手が掴めなくて
findings.explanation: Haruki apologizes for being boring because it has been so long since he made casual telephone conversation that he cannot get the hang of it. The English says the long interval made him unable to resist answering, an unrelated impulse that neither explains his poor storytelling nor answers Koharu's complaint.
findings.japanese:
「つまんなくて悪かったな。
電話で雑談するの、本当に久しぶりだから
勝手が掴めなくて」
findings.todokanai: "Sorry if I'm boring you. It's been a long time since I've had a casual conversation on the phone, so I just couldn't resist answering your call."
